replace-the-in-cell-selection-ring-inset.text: Replace the in-cell selection ring / inset shadow (#selection-ring) with a zoom-aware overlay drawn OUTSIDE the cell interior so a selected cell's full color stays visible and comfortably targetable at paint zoom. The overlay must share the same camera transform used for rendering and pointer hit testing, sit above the board without capturing paint gestures, and keep keyboard navigation and touch drag/pinch from ever submitting paint. Keep the selected color swatch visible next to the board. Acceptance: at paint zoom a chosen cell shows its entire color with the indicator fully outside the cell; adjacent painted cells still touch with no unintended gaps; corners/center still map correctly after zoom/pan/resize; touch drag and pinch do not paint; arrow-key navigation remains usable and moves the external indicator with the selection.

make-painted-cells-render-as-exact-seam-.text: Make painted cells render as exact, seam-free squares at every zoom level and device pixel ratio so a chosen cell reads as one fully colored square. Board review acceptance: 'adjacent painted cells touch without unintended gaps'. The canvas renderer `web/src/render-board.ts` currently fills rectangles (`fillRect(x * CELL, y * CELL, CELL, CELL)`, CELL = 4) into a container-scaled canvas, so cell edges can leave background seams or shaved/blurred boundaries once the board is scaled into the zoomed viewport or shown on fractional-DPR displays. Correct the renderer so that: (a) neighbouring painted cells share an edge with no background-colored seam and no overlapping or anti-aliased boundary at overview zoom, painting zoom, and fit-to-wall; (b) cell edges land on device pixels (crisp) at DPR 1, 2 and fractional scaling, including when the zoom transform is fractional; (c) rendering stays a pure function of board state plus camera so it is unit-testable without DOM layout. Keep the logical 128x128 board, the eight-color palette indices, the on-chain pixel format, the existing `get_pixels` page size, and the camera/hit-test/wall-page modules untouched - keep the fix confined to the renderer module and its test. If a camera-side rounding change turns out to be genuinely required, stop and report it in the task result rather than editing the wall page or camera module. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm ci` before any verification. Add or extend unit tests in `web/src/render-board.test.ts` covering the seam/gap invariant: adjacent filled cells produce contiguous coverage with no uncovered background row/column, painted coverage equals cell area times painted cell count, and scaled cell rectangles are pixel-aligned across a zoom x DPR matrix (overview, painting zoom, fit-to-wall; DPR 1 and 2).

complete-the-board-viewport-and-toolbar-.text: Complete the board viewport and toolbar for the core painting moment on a phone. At a 390px-wide viewport the palette and the Place action must sit within reach of the board - visible without a long scroll and not pushed below the fold - with a compact connection/freshness indicator next to the board. Move contract/schema/rules/state/debug text out of the primary presentation into an expandable About/details panel so the wall is the primary surface. Label any local sample art used for visual testing as demo data. Draw the selection indicator outside the chosen cell (offset ring/overlay) so the whole cell interior stays colored. Keep pointer hit testing aligned with the rendered grid after zoom, pan and resize (all four corners and the center map correctly), and make touch drag/pinch pan or zoom without ever submitting paint; keyboard cell navigation must keep working. Reuse the existing camera transform, hit test and pending-paint layer; do not change the contract, the shared constants/palette, the draw submit path, or the placement-outcome status model. Do not add function-call key creation, change sign-in, or touch wallet/deployment code - connection state is only displayed. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm ci` before any verification. Add or extend tests under `web/src/pages/wall/` for selection-indicator geometry (indicator sits outside the cell, cell interior not obscured) and for tap-vs-drag discrimination (a drag or pinch produces zero draw submissions while a tap on a cell selects/places as before).

at-paint-zoom-a-cell-must-read-as-a-full.text: At paint zoom a cell must read as a full, crisp square of roughly 16–24 CSS px on desktop and on a 390 px viewport; adjacent painted cells must share edges with no seam, hairline, or blur; the selection indicator must be drawn outside the chosen cell's bounds so the cell's own color fills its interior at full size. Implement this in the viewport/display layer — size the canvas backing store from the active camera zoom and devicePixelRatio and keep one shared transform used by rendering, hit testing, and overlays — rather than relying on the bitmap cell constant that CSS scaling negates. Keep the 128x128 logical board. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm ci` from a clean tree before running tests or the build. Constraints: do not change the contract, `shared/**`, the palette or overwrite rules, or wallet/signing/connection modules; confine edits to the renderer, selection/overlay, camera-transform modules and their tests.

make-painting-at-zoom-precise-and-seam-f.text: Make painting at zoom precise and seam-free without touching the presentation CSS or the contract. Deliverables: (1) at paint zoom each cell renders as a complete edge-to-edge rectangle so adjacent painted cells share a boundary with no visible seam, background line, or partially filled interior at zoom levels 1x/2x/4x/8x and device pixel ratios 1/2/3; (2) a click/tap at paint zoom selects and places on the cell actually under the pointer, not a neighbour, at every zoom level, pan offset and window resize; (3) pan, pinch and drag gestures never submit a paint — only a tap that resolves to a cell may select/place, and a drag that ends on a different cell than it started must not paint. Approach: keep the 128x128 logical board, the existing fillRect(x * CELL, y * CELL, CELL, CELL) geometry and the existing camera transform; do NOT change the bitmap CELL constant and do NOT edit web/src/style.css. Instead own canvas sizing in web/src/main.ts so the canvas backing store equals the displayed CSS size multiplied by devicePixelRatio (the bitmap is never upscaled by CSS), and derive pointer hit-testing, cell rects and any selection geometry from one shared device-pixel-snapped rect computation in web/src/render-board.ts. Add unit tests in web/src/render-board.test.ts for the rect math and hit-testing across those zoom/DPR combinations, including a corner cell, the centre cell, a resize case, and a drag-ends-on-another-cell case that must not submit a paint. Do not change board dimensions, palette, contract metadata handling, submit/queue logic or wallet calls. Environment: run `cd web && npm ci` first; verification runs from the repository root.

on-a-390-px-wide-viewport-reference-390x.text: On a 390 px-wide viewport (reference 390x844) the palette and the Place/confirm action sit in a bottom control bar within thumb reach and never overlap the board's paint target area; the board keeps the largest remaining height above the bar and safe-area insets are respected. The selected-cell indicator is drawn outside the chosen cell so the cell's interior stays fully colored at every zoom level (no border or inset shadow over the cell). Contract/schema/debug text stays out of the primary view and connection/freshness status stays compact. Approach: implement as HTML structure plus CSS layout only, in web/index.html and web/src/style.css (sticky/safe-area bottom bar, flex sizing so the board fills the space above it, selection indicator positioned outside the cell rect). Do NOT change submit/queue logic, wallet calls, contract reads, the draw path, or the wall page module's lifecycle or its tests — the previous attempt edited a wall-mount dispose test and was blocked; this attempt leaves that module and its tests untouched. Label any placeholder/demo art used for visual checking as demo data. Environment: run `cd web && npm ci` first; verification runs from the repository root.

deliver-device-pixel-accurate-board-rend.text: Deliver device-pixel-accurate board rendering so the paint moment is crisp and precisely targetable. The wall canvas backing store must equal its CSS size x devicePixelRatio and be refreshed on window resize and DPR change; confirmed cells must be drawn as integer-aligned rectangles covering the whole logical cell so adjacent painted cells touch with no seam, blur, or partially colored edge. This must hold at fit-to-wall zoom, at paint zoom (~16-24 screen px per cell), at DPR 1/2/3, and after pan/resize, with all four corners and the centre mapping correctly. Keep the merged zoom/pan camera transform as the single board->screen mapping and keep render-board.ts's existing public API plus the draw submission path unchanged. Add unit tests for the logical->device pixel mapping and for the full-cell-coverage invariant. No contract, palette, wallet, or deployment edits.

deliver-an-external-zoom-aware-selection.text: Deliver an external, zoom-aware selection indicator and hover preview so the chosen cell's color is never hidden. The selection indicator must be drawn outside the chosen cell's interior (offset and scaled with the camera transform) rather than as an inward border/inset shadow over it, and must remain legible and correctly positioned at fit-to-wall zoom, at paint zoom, and on the 390 px mobile layout. Hovering or selecting a cell must preview the currently selected palette color in a separate preview layer that is visually distinct from confirmed art and from pending paint, never covering a confirmed cell's color. Add unit tests asserting the indicator geometry has zero overlap with the chosen cell's interior and that the preview layer is not part of the confirmed-pixel layer. Preserve the merged zoom/pan camera transform contract and the toolbar layout from head commit 245f9c7; no contract, palette, wallet, or deployment edits.

make-the-chosen-cell-crisp-and-precisely.text: Make the chosen cell crisp and precisely targetable at paint zoom, with the cell's color never obscured. Size the wall canvas backing store to CSS size x devicePixelRatio so cells rasterize crisply, and ensure adjacent painted cells touch exactly (no gaps or 1px overlaps between neighbours) at any zoom level, pan offset or resize. Expose the selection indicator as a screen-space rect computed from the shared camera transform so it is drawn outside the chosen cell's interior (zoom-aware ring/border) and never covers the stored color; style it in the stylesheet used today. Cover both with unit tests: indicator rect lies outside the cell rect at overview zoom, paint zoom and DPR 1/2/3, and neighbour cell rects are edge-adjacent with zero gap at those zooms.

make-painting-on-a-phone-safe-and-honest.text: Make painting on a phone safe and honest: distinguish tap from drag with pointer events so panning, pinching and any two-pointer gesture never submit a draw - only an explicit Place action (or an explicitly enabled direct-paint mode) submits, and keyboard selection/placement keeps working unchanged. Render pending paint in a separate client layer that is visibly different from confirmed art (e.g. distinct badge/outline/dimmed treatment) and is cleared or reconciled by the existing submitted/confirmed/confirmation-delayed/failed/overwritten outcome states rather than being silently merged into confirmed cells. Add tests that a drag sequence, a pinch sequence and a wheel/pan gesture on the wall surface produce zero submitted draws, that a single tap plus Place produces exactly one, and that pending cells are marked as pending and never counted as confirmed.

guarantee-that-pan-pinch-and-drag-never-.text: Guarantee that pan, pinch and drag never submit paint and that queued paint is visibly distinct from confirmed art. (a) Extract gesture classification into a standalone pure module web/src/gesture.ts that converts pointer events into tap vs drag vs pan vs pinch using a movement/time threshold and pointer-count, with its own unit tests in web/src/gesture.test.ts. (b) Wire that classifier into web/src/pages/wall/mount-wall.ts with a minimal diff so only a deliberate tap (or the explicit Place action) enqueues a draw, and any gesture that moved beyond the threshold, used multiple pointers or began on the pan surface is discarded without a submit. (c) Render queued/pending cells in a separate client-side layer above confirmed pixels, derived from the existing paint queue and the existing submitted/confirmed/confirmation-delayed/failed/overwritten outcome states, with styling in web/src/style.css that is clearly different from confirmed art. (d) An uncertain request must never be auto-resubmitted when refresh or reconnect replaces board state. Do NOT modify AGENT.md, fix_plan.md or any repo-root document; no contract, wallet or economy files. Verify with web unit tests and the production build.
